The Centrale Raad van Beroep is one of the four highest administrative courts and rules on appeal in cases on social insurance, social provisions and civil service matters. The Raad is based in Utrecht.

The College van Beroep voor het bedrijfsleven is the highest administrative court in economic administrative law and sits in Den Haag. Among other things, it hears cases on competition, market regulation, subsidies, fertilisers and financial supervision.

The Dienst van het Koninklijk Huis supports the King, Queen Máxima and Princess Beatrix in their work and private lives. The service also supports the other members of the Royal House in their duties. Its nearly 300 staff work in Den Haag, Amsterdam, Apeldoorn and Baarn; the grootmeester (Grand Master) heads the royal household.

The Hoge Raad der Nederlanden is the highest court in civil, criminal and tax cases. It is a court of cassation: it assesses whether lower courts applied the law correctly and whether the procedure was followed correctly. The Hoge Raad is also the court of cassation for Aruba, Curacao, Sint Maarten and Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba.

The Kabinet van de Koning supports the King in carrying out his constitutional duties. It handles and prepares the King's contacts with the minister-president and the other ministers and state secretaries. It processes the laws, general administrative orders and royal decrees presented for signature and handles petitions from citizens.

The cabinet consists of the ministers and the state secretaries. The ministers and the state secretaries are appointed and dismissed by royal decree. The current kabinet-Jetten was sworn in on 23 February 2026 and has 18 ministers and 10 state secretaries.

The Kanselarij der Nederlandse Orden houses and supports the Kapittel voor de Civiele Orden and the Kapittel der Militaire Willems-Orde in their advice on proposals for decorations. The organisation manages the insignia, keeps registers of decorated persons and guards the purity and dignity of the orders. Its history goes back to 1815, when the Militaire Willems-Orde and the Orde van de Nederlandse Leeuw were established; the Kanselier der Nederlandse Orden is at its head.
The persons entitled to vote for the Tweede Kamer: Dutch nationals aged eighteen and over who are not excluded from the right to vote. They elect the 150 members of the Tweede Kamer.

The Kiesraad is responsible for elections in the Netherlands and ensures that they are fair and transparent. Statutory task: The Kiesraad has the following tasks:* advising the government and both Kamers der Staten-Generaal on technical implementation matters concerning the right to vote or elections (article A2 Kieswet);* acting as the central electoral committee for the elections of the members of:
a. the Tweede Kamer (article E II, second paragraph, Kieswet);
b. the Eerste Kamer (article S I, first paragraph, Kieswet);
c. the European Parliament (article Y9, first paragraph, Kieswet);* advising government bodies, political parties, media and citizens during elections and acting as an expert adviser in legal proceedings.

The ministerie van Algemene Zaken coordinates government policy and central government communication and safeguards their unity and continuity. It supports the minister-president in preparing and carrying out cabinet policy. The ministry was established by royal decree of 3 July 1937 and is based in Den Haag.

The ministerie van Binnenlandse Zaken en Koninkrijksrelaties works on democracy, public administration, fundamental rights, housing and spatial planning, and on relations within the Kingdom. Since the departmental reorganisation of 23 February 2026, public housing, spatial planning and digital affairs also fall within the department. The ministry is based in Den Haag.

The ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken coordinates and carries out the foreign policy of the Netherlands, from Den Haag and through embassies, consulates and other missions in about 150 countries. It promotes Dutch interests, contributes to international stability and helps Dutch nationals abroad. The department has existed since 1798.

The ministerie van Defensie protects the security of the Netherlands and its allies and contributes to the international legal order and stability. The armed forces also support society during disasters and crises. The department consists of the central staff in Den Haag and the operational units of the navy, army and air force, the marechaussee and supporting commands.

The ministerie van Economische Zaken en Klimaat works towards a productive, resilient and sustainable economy. The department is responsible for entrepreneurship, innovation, climate and energy, digitalisation and the management of raw materials. On 23 February 2026 its name changed from Economische Zaken to Economische Zaken en Klimaat; tasks in the fields of climate, green growth and the circular economy were transferred to it at that time.

The ministerie van Financiën manages the public finances and is responsible for financially sound central government. It draws up the Rijksbegroting, is responsible for the tax system and supervises the financial sector. The ministry has existed since 1798, which makes it one of the oldest departments.

The ministerie van Infrastructuur en Waterstaat works on accessibility, safe dikes and clean air, soil and water. The department is responsible for the road, rail and water networks and for the management of Rijkswaterstaat. It also works towards a good living environment and the economical use of raw materials.

The ministerie van Justitie en Veiligheid is responsible for the legal order and for a safer and more just society. It works with municipalities, the Openbaar Ministerie, the police and other partners on law enforcement, protection and migration. Since 23 February 2026, asylum and migration also fall within this department.

The ministerie van Landbouw, Visserij, Voedselzekerheid en Natuur works for sustainable and safe food, healthy nature and a vital countryside. The department focuses on agriculture, fisheries, food security, nature and nitrogen, for current and future generations. It is based in Den Haag.

The ministerie van Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap ensures good education, room for science and a free cultural sector. It sets frameworks for and funds education and culture policy and science. The department has had its current name since 2003, when it moved from Zoetermeer to Den Haag.

The ministerie van Sociale Zaken en Werkgelegenheid works for fair, healthy and safe work and for financial security for everyone. It is responsible for social security, the labour market and income policy. The ministry is based in Den Haag.

The ministerie van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport works for good and affordable care and support. It encourages a healthy lifestyle, sufficient exercise and sport and is responsible for the healthcare system. The department is based in Den Haag.

The Nederlandse Emissieautoriteit (NEa) is the independent national authority for the implementation and supervision of market instruments that contribute to a climate-neutral society. The NEa is a so-called small independent administrative body (zbo). This means that the board is a zbo, while the working organisation is an agency of the Ministerie van Economische Zaken en Klimaat (EZK). The main clients of the organisation are the ministries of EZK, Infrastructuur en Waterstaat (IenW) and Financiën (MinFin). The NEa is based in Den Haag and has more than 140 employees.

The Openbaar Ministerie is charged with the criminal law enforcement of the legal order and with other tasks laid down by law. National leadership rests with the College van procureurs-generaal; the OM consists of the parket-generaal, the arrondissementsparketten, the landelijk parket, the functioneel parket, the parket centrale verwerking and the ressortsparketten.

The Stichting Centraal Orgaan Voorraadvorming Aardolieproducten (COVA) is a legal entity with a statutory task. COVA is the central, independent organisation that holds strategic oil stocks for the Netherlands on behalf of the minister of Klimaat en Groene Groei. The mandatory oil stock consists of at most 2/3 crude oil and at least 1/3 refined product. The product stock consists of petrol, diesel and kerosene, divided in proportion to domestic use.

The Innovam Branche Kwalificatie Instituut (IBKI) is responsible for developing and administering theory and practical exams in the mobility sector, for example for people who want to obtain or keep the authority to carry out a periodic vehicle inspection (APK) of motor vehicles. IBKI is a trade name of the [Stichting Vakopleiding Automobiel- en Motorrijwielbedrijf (VAM)](https://organisaties.overheid.nl/30133473/Stichting_VAM__Opleidingsinstituur_voor_het_Motorvoertuig-__Tweewieler-_en_Aanverwant_Bedrijf), also known as Innovam.

ProRail is the railway infrastructure manager. This means that we are responsible for the maintenance, renewal, expansion and safety of the Dutch railway network. As an independent party we allocate the capacity on 7,000 kilometres of track, manage all train traffic (160 million kilometres per year) and build and manage stations. We do this with attention to our society and with an eye to the future. ProRail stands for sustainable mobility. Through innovation we make it possible for more people to travel by train and for more goods to be transported by rail. ProRail is an unlisted company. The company's board consists of three statutory directors. The supervisory board oversees it. The Dutch State, through Railinfratrust B.V., is the sole shareholder of ProRail B.V. The shareholding is held by the ministry of Infrastructuur en Waterstaat.

The Raad stands for a safe and just society. To that end, the Raad contributes to the quality of law enforcement by supervising, from an independent position, the functioning of the justice chain and providing insight into it.

The organisation is subsidised by, among others, DGPJS. Slachtofferhulp Nederland stands up for the interests and rights of victims of a crime or a traffic accident. At the 75 Buro's Slachtofferhulp, 1500 volunteers and 250 professionals work every day to help victims. The services consist of practical and legal advice and emotional support. In the media and in politics, Slachtofferhulp Nederland acts as an advocate. The organisation encourages research and lobbies politically with the aim of strengthening the position of victims.

Defensie protects what we Dutch hold dear. We fight for a world in which people can live in freedom and safety, because we are convinced that every person deserves that. That is our mission, and for that we go on missions. The armed forces have 3 main tasks. These are: protecting our own territory and that of allies; promoting the (international) legal order and stability; supporting civil authorities and providing assistance in disasters and crises.

The College donorgegevens kunstmatige bevruchting (Cdkb) carries out the Wet donorgegevens kunstmatige bevruchting. Since 2004, the data of sperm, egg and embryo donors have been registered nationally. The Cdkb is responsible for managing these data and provides them on request to the donor child, the parents or the general practitioner. The board of the Cdkb has transferred a number of implementing tasks to the Centraal Informatiepunt Beroepen Gezondheidszorg (CIBG), including the registration of donor data, the secretariat of the Cdkb and the provision of information. The Cdkb nevertheless is and remains responsible for the data and decides on requests for donor data that it receives. The CIBG is an agency of the Ministerie van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport (VWS).

About Halt: Halt focuses on preventing, combating and punishing youth crime. Halt has the statutory task of punishing transgressive behaviour by young people. About 17,000 young people a year receive a Halt penalty. Halt is also active in prevention. Halt gives many information sessions at schools, sports clubs or in the neighbourhood. Halt also offers tailored interventions and projects. Halt is a connecting partner between the family, the world of juvenile criminal law, the municipality and organisations that young people deal with. In this way Halt actively contributes to a safe and liveable environment. Organisation: since 1 January 2013, Halt has been one organisation with teams throughout the country. In this way Halt continues to meet local wishes. Halt joins forces into one vital organisation that has more clout and works efficiently. Halt is a foundation with a director/board member and a supervisory board. The organisation consists of regional teams (in line with the judicial map and the 10 police regions) and a national office, each with a team manager. Funding: Halt carries out the Halt penalty under the responsibility of the Openbaar Ministerie. The ministry of Veiligheid en Justitie funds the execution of the Halt penalty. Halt carries out prevention assignments on behalf of municipalities and other clients, such as central government, provinces, care and welfare organisations, sports federations and schools. TASK: preventing, combating and punishing transgressive behaviour by young people.

TASK: offering programmes aimed at resocialisation, like the two partners mentioned earlier, to people who have come into contact with the justice system. Deploying expertise and manpower to prevent repeat offences. It acts as quickly as possible, preferably immediately after someone has been arrested. It can play a role in all phases of the legal process. The Reclassering carries out three core tasks: investigation, information and reporting to the justice authorities on the person of the offender and the circumstances of the offending behaviour. That information can play a role in the further handling of the case by the justice system; guidance and supervision. Guidance and supervision can be carried out either voluntarily or in a mandatory framework (judgment). The Reclassering carries out activities that enable the suspect to better handle his responsibility in society; offering early assistance to detainees; offering reintegration programmes to detainees; developing and offering community sentences and penitentiary programmes. Community sentences can be divided into work and learning sentences. They are imposed by the judge, and the probation service provides organisation and guidance. When taking part in a penitentiary programme, a detainee spends the last part of his prison sentence outside the walls of the institution, in his home environment, under strict guidance and supervision. In this way the detainee slowly learns to deal with an increasing degree of freedom. Explanation: the stichting Reclassering Nederland (SRN) was founded in 1995 and brings together all institutions engaged in probation work in the Netherlands, namely: Stichting Reclassering Nederland, the probation department of the Leger des Heils, and the addiction care institutions united in GGZ Nederland. The bundling of probation work was started to safeguard the quality and optimisation of assistance to people who come into contact with the justice system.

Independent planning bureau that monitors, explains and explores the quality of life and society in the Netherlands.

Representative body (parliament) of the country of Aruba, elected by the residents for four years (Statuut art. 46; gobierno.aw). 21 seats, after the election of 06-12-2024: AVP 9, MEP 8, FUTURO Aruba 3, PPA 1. The parliamentary year starts on the second Tuesday of September.

Representative body (parliament) of the country of Curaçao, 21 members, elected at the election of 21-03-2025 and installed on 11-05-2025. Composition: MFK 13, PNP 4, PAR 2, MAN 2. The Staten scrutinise the government and hold it to account (parlamento.cw).

Representative body (parliament) of the country of Sint Maarten, 15 elected members (sxmparliament.org). Established on 10-10-2010, the day on which the country of Sint Maarten gained status equalis within the Kingdom.
The Tweede Kamer is the directly elected part of the Staten-Generaal. It consists of 150 members, scrutinises the government and, together with the Eerste Kamer, adopts laws.
Scientific advisory council of the government on strategic issues with important long-term consequences.

Statutory task: acting as an independent assessing body in conformity assessments of measuring instruments. The work they perform may differ per conformity assessment but includes, among other things, assessing quality systems, issuing type examination or design examination certificates and inspecting measuring instruments.

Airport Coordination Netherlands (ACNL) is the body in the Netherlands responsible for the seasonal planning of flights, as well as allocating airport slots (arrival and departure times of aircraft) to airlines and supervising the use of these slots. ACNL performs these tasks, in accordance with European regulations, for the airports Amsterdam Airport Schiphol, Rotterdam The Hague Airport and Eindhoven Airport.

Statutory task: Airport Coordination Netherlands (ACNL) has the following tasks and powers:* allocating slots to airlines;* studying and advising on developments in the field of aircraft movements;* reporting periodically to the ministry of Infrastructuur en Waterstaat.

Argonaut Advies B.V. is the medical advisory partner for municipalities, health insurers, care offices and central governments and is authorised to exercise public authority in the public task of issuing assessments for a high personal kilometre budget for supra-regional transport for people with a mobility impairment (the Valys-regeling).

Statutory task: as an independent administrative body (zbo), Argonaut Advies B.V. is authorised to exercise public authority in the public task of issuing assessments for a high personal kilometre budget for supra-regional transport for people with a mobility impairment (the Valys-regeling). This zbo task is deciding on applications for a high personal kilometre budget for people who, because of a mobility impairment, cannot travel by train (not even with an escort). Argonaut's status as a zbo for this task is based on the [existing case law](https://uitspraken.rechtspraak.nl/details?id=ECLI:NL:CRVB:2018:2554) of the Centrale Raad van Beroep (CRvB).

ASR Wlz-uitvoerder B.V. is an implementer of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz), as referred to in article 4.1.1 of that law.

Statutory task: ASR Wlz-uitvoerder B.V. is responsible for carrying out the tasks described in section 2 of chapter 4 (articles 4.2.1 to 4.2.6 inclusive) of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz).

The Autoriteit Consument en Markt (ACM) was established on 1 April 2013 and independently supervises competition, consumer law and several specific (business) sectors. The aim of the ACM is the proper, fair functioning of markets for both consumers and businesses. The ACM arose from a merger of the Consumentenautoriteit, the Nederlandse Mededingingsautoriteit (NMa) and the Onafhankelijke Post en Telecommunicatie Autoriteit (OPTA). The supervisory tasks of the ACM cover both European and Caribbean Netherlands.

Statutory task: the ACM is charged with tasks (mainly compliance supervision and administrative enforcement) under the following legislation:* Wet handhaving consumentenbescherming;* Mededingingswet;* Telecommunicatiewet;* Postwet 2009;* Elektriciteitswet 1998;* Gaswet;* transport legislation (Wet personenvervoer 2000, Loodsenwet, Spoorwegwet, Wet luchtvaart and Scheepvaartverkeerswet).

The Autoriteit Nucleaire Veiligheid en Stralingsbescherming (ANVS) ensures that nuclear safety and radiation protection in the Netherlands meet the highest standards. To that end, the ANVS draws up rules, grants permits, supervises compliance with them and can take enforcement action. Until 2015, the various government tasks and knowledge about the nuclear sector were spread across different bodies. All this knowledge and expertise is now brought together in the ANVS. Since 1 August 2017, the ANVS has been an independent administrative body (zbo). This allows decisions to be taken independently. The ANVS falls under the responsibility of the minister of Infrastructuur en Waterstaat.

Statutory task: the ANVS grants permits, registers notifications and registers and recognises experts and radiation physicians. In addition, the ANVS is responsible for supervision and for taking measures when necessary for nuclear safety or radiation protection. Furthermore, the ANVS, together with a number of partners, ensures that the Netherlands is as well prepared as possible for radiation incidents and nuclear accidents. The Autoriteit also has a task in developing policy for nuclear safety and radiation protection, including policy for radioactive waste. It prepares laws and regulations or advises on them. Internationally, the ANVS works with various foreign governments, authorities and organisations such as the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA).

The Autoriteit online Terroristisch en Kinderpornografisch Materiaal (ATKM) oversees the detection and removal of internet material of a terrorist or child pornographic nature, so that it cannot be spread further.

Statutory task: the main tasks of the Autoriteit online Terroristisch en Kinderpornografisch Materiaal (ATKM) are:* detecting terrorist and child pornographic material on the internet;* ensuring the rapid removal of such material by issuing removal orders to hosting service providers;* countering the spread of such material, in cooperation with the internet sector.

The Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP) was established and designated as the supervisory authority for the Algemene verordening gegevensbescherming (AVG) and the Uitvoeringswet AVG (UAVG). The AP is both an advisory board and an independent administrative body.

Statutory task: the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP) is responsible for, among other things:* supervising the processing of personal data in accordance with the provisions of and under the law;* supervising the processing of personal data in the Netherlands when the processing takes place in accordance with the law of another country of the European Union;* advising on bills and draft general administrative orders that relate wholly or largely to the processing of personal data;* assessing codes of conduct;* conducting prior investigations into processing operations with special risks;* advising on permits for transferring personal data to countries outside the European Union;* handling complaints and requests from data subjects and other interested parties;* various tasks under the Wet politiegegevens and other special legislation;* various international law tasks related to the above.

This is a cluster consisting of independent administrative bodies (zbo's) that do not fall under the Kaderwet zelfstandige bestuursorganen. The underlying parts of this cluster are therefore not named in the Register van Overheidsorganisaties.

The Bedrijfsvoering en strategie (BVS) department is an organisational unit of the Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS).

Statutory task: the Bedrijfsvoering en strategie (BVS) department of the CBS consists of the departments below, each divided into a number of teams: BSB (Strategie en bestuursadvisering):* BSA (Algemeen)* BBE (Beleid)* BIA (Interne auditdienst) BCB (Control & bedrijfsadministraties):* BBA (Bedrijfsadministraties)* BPC (Planning & control) BPO (Personeel en organisatie):* BPD (Personeel en organisatie Den Haag)* BPH (Personeel en organisatie Heerlen)* BCA (CBS Academy) BFB (Facilitair Bedrijf):* BRO (Regieorganisatie)* BUO (Uitvoeringsorganisatie)* BIH (Informatiehuishouding) BBM (Ondersteuning & informatiemanagement):* BBM (Ondersteuning & informatiemanagement)* BMO (Managementondersteuning) The departments and teams are taken from the [CBS-organogram](https://www.cbs.nl/-/media/_pdf/organogram-nl.pdf).

This is a cluster consisting of independent administrative bodies (zbo's) that do not fall under the Kaderwet zelfstandige bestuursorganen. The underlying parts of this cluster are therefore not named in the Register van Overheidsorganisaties.

Statutory task: issuing an inspection certificate for vessels in Rhine navigation. This involves assessing whether a vessel complies with the guidelines and poses no danger to the safety of a person on board, or to shipping. In practice this concerns only the Commissie van Deskundigen (of the reglement onderzoek schepen op de Rijn).

On the basis of the Wet op de architectentitel, we share responsibility for the professional competence of 14,000 interior architects, architects, garden and landscape architects and urban planners (referred to as 'architect'). In doing so, we pursue the objectives of the Wet op de architectentitel: ensuring competent professional practice by the architect and thereby promoting the quality of the landscape and the built environment, implementing European directives for the four titles, and protecting the consumer.

Statutory task: the Wet op de architectentitel assigns the Bureau Architectenregister (BA) four categories of tasks and powers:* managing the register;* work as competent authority;* work relating to schemes of the Wet op de architectentitel;* other statutory tasks and powers. In addition, the Architectenregister carries out the independent route of the Beroepservaringperiode and, together with the College van Rijksbouwmeester & Rijksadviseurs, periodically coordinates research into the state of architecture.

The Bureau Beheer Landbouwgronden (BBL) acquires real estate and passes it on to government and other organisations, so that government goals in the landscape in the areas of nature, agriculture, recreation, landscape, water and environment can be achieved.

Statutory task: the Bureau Beheer Landbouwgronden (BBL) is charged with acquiring real estate that is passed on to government and other organisations, which use it to achieve government goals in rural areas relating to the themes of nature, agriculture, recreation, landscape, water and environment. As a separate independent administrative body, the BBL falls under the policy and system responsibility of the ministry of Landbouw, Visserij, Voedselzekerheid en Natuur.

BFT independently supervises compliance with laws and regulations by notaries and bailiffs. BFT also supervises compliance with the Wet ter voorkoming van witwassen en financieren van terrorisme (Wwft) by financial and legal service providers. Our goal? To promote legal certainty and financial integrity in the Netherlands. This means that financial and legal service providers are aware of laws and regulations and apply them in daily practice. To achieve this, we carry out both preventive and repressive activities. In the area of prevention, we provide information and hold conversations. Through cooperation with chain partners, we also try to respond to signals and identify risks in time. On the other hand, we carry out investigations in response to signals or risks. Such investigations can lead to enforcement, ranging from a warning conversation to a fine or a disciplinary complaint. To realise our goal, we have formulated three ambitions: steering for lasting impact, combating subversion and responding to technological developments.

Statutory task: The Bureau Financieel Toezicht exercises financial supervision of notaries and bailiffs. It also supervises compliance with the Wet ter voorkoming van witwassen en financieren van terrorisme (Wwft) by notaries, accountants, lawyers, tax advisers and other financial and legal service providers.

Statutory task: The CAK is charged with: * setting and collecting the personal contributions referred to in article 3.2.5 of the Wet langdurige zorg;* setting and collecting the personal contributions referred to in article 2.1.4 of the Wet maatschappelijke ondersteuning 2015* making payments to care providers on behalf of a WLZ-uitvoerder or the Zorginstituut, which the WLZ-uitvoerders or the Zorginstituut owe under the implementation of this law* the tasks relating to the measures aimed at insuring the uninsured, referred to in section 2.4 of the Zorgverzekeringswet* levying and collecting the administrative-law premium referred to in article 18d or article 18e of the Zorgverzekeringswet* providing the contribution referred to in article 34a of the Zorgverzekeringswet* the tasks referred to in article 69 of the Zorgverzekeringswet* the tasks relating to conscientious objectors, referred to in article 70 of the Zorgverzekeringswet, and - providing the contributions referred to in article 122a of the Zorgverzekeringswet ('Uninsurable foreign nationals')

The CBS communicatie en nieuws (CCN) department is an organisational unit of the Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS).

Statutory task: The CBS communicatie en nieuws (CCN) department of the CBS consists of the teams below:* CST (Staff)* CDV (Design & visualisation)* CRM (Editorial & media)* CCC (Corporate communication)* CRS (Central coordination & services)* COP (Online platforms)The teams are taken from the [CBS-organogram](https://www.cbs.nl/-/media/_pdf/organogram-nl.pdf).

The Centraal Bureau Rijvaardigheidsbewijzen (CBR) is a national organisation that assesses the driving ability and medical fitness of drivers of motor vehicles, as well as the professional competence of professionals in the transport and logistics sector. The CBR does this on behalf of the minister of Infrastructuur en Waterstaat. The CBR has a head office in Rijswijk and 54 exam locations spread across the country. This allows the CBR to contribute to road safety throughout the Netherlands.

Statutory task: The main tasks of the CBR are:* conducting theory and practical exams for various driving licence categories;* certifying refresher courses for drivers in goods and passenger transport;* assessing the fitness to drive of both citizens and professionals;* investigating the fitness to drive or driving ability of drivers when unfitness is suspected;* imposing educational measures, for example in the area of alcohol and traffic.

The Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS) collects data from persons and businesses and processes this data into statistics. The statistics of the CBS cover a large number of different subjects (for example housing, work, health and the economy) and are publicly available.

Statutory task: The Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek (CBS) has the following tasks:* carrying out statistical research on behalf of the government for practice, policy and science;* publishing the statistics that result from the research mentioned above.In addition to its responsibility for the national (official) statistics, the CBS is also responsible for compiling European (Community) statistics.

COA stands for Centraal Orgaan opvang asielzoekers. The COA is an independent administrative body. Until the introduction of the Regeling Opvang Asielzoekers (1987), there was no official asylum reception in the Netherlands. From 1992, the making of asylum reception independent was worked out further into the Wet Centraal Orgaan opvang asielzoekers. That law has been in force since 1 juli 1994. Since 1994 we have been responsible for the reception and guidance of asylum seekers in the Netherlands. Furthermore, the board is the one responsible for carrying out the tasks as described in the Wet COA. The powers of the board are also set out in the Bevoegdhedenregeling COA.

Statutory task: Organising, in a businesslike manner, a humane and sober initial stay for varying numbers of asylum seekers who come to the Netherlands, in such a way that their arrival and initial stay are manageable for government and society.

The CCD is a committee made up of external members. They are supported by a secretariat, the so-called ondersteunend bureau dierproeven en alternatieven (OBDA). The staff are made available by the minister of LVVN and are employed by the Rijksdienst voor Ondernemend Nederland (RVO).

Statutory task: The CCD grants licences for carrying out animal experiments on the basis of advice from the Dierexperimentencommissies (DEC).

The Centrale Commissie Mensgebonden Onderzoek (CCMO) safeguards the protection of research subjects involved in medical scientific research, by reviewing against the statutory provisions laid down for such research and by taking into account the various developments within medical science.

Statutory task: The CCMO has the following tasks and powers:* supervising the review by medical ethics committees of medical scientific research involving humans in the Netherlands;* reviewing forms of research as described in article 2 of the Wet medisch-wetenschappelijk onderzoek met mensen and article 3 of the Embryowet;* handling administrative appeals by interested parties against assessments by medical ethics review committees;* registering medical scientific research involving humans.

This is a cluster made up of independent administrative bodies that do not fall under the Kaderwet zelfstandige bestuursorganen. The underlying units of this cluster are therefore not named in the Register van Overheidsorganisaties.

The CIZ is the successor to the private-law zbo Centrum Indicatiestelling Zorg, founded in 2005.

Statutory task: The CIZ issues eligibility decisions that give insured persons access to care under the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz) and the Wet zorg en dwang (Wzd).

The College donorgegevens kunstmatige bevruchting (Cdkb) carries out the Wet donorgegevens kunstmatige bevruchting. Since 2004, the data of sperm, egg and embryo donors have been registered nationally. The Cdkb is responsible for managing this data and provides it on request to the donor child, the parents or the general practitioner. The board of the Cdkb has transferred a number of implementation tasks to the Centraal Informatiepunt Beroepen Gezondheidszorg (CIBG), including the registration of donor data, the secretariat of the Cdkb and the provision of information. The Cdkb nevertheless is and remains responsible for the data and decides on requests received for donor data. The CIBG is an agency of the Ministerie van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport (VWS).

Statutory task: The College donorgegevens kunstmatige bevruchting (Cdkb) is responsible for carrying out the Wet donorgegevens kunstmatige bevruchting (Wdkb). To that end, the Cdkb carries out the following tasks:* storing and managing donor data. The data are stored in a central database and kept for at least eighty years;* providing donor data on request to the child, the parents and the general practitioner of the donor child;* ensuring expert guidance when the data are provided (in cooperation with Fiom);* issuing parenthood declarations for co-motherhood;* providing information about the Wdkb.

The Nederlands Register Gerechtelijk Deskundigen (NRGD) is a register of certified experts who report in criminal cases. The College gerechtelijk deskundigen forms the board of the NRGD. The College is an independent administrative body (zbo) that falls under the ministerie van Justitie en Veiligheid.

Statutory task: The Nederlands Register Gerechtelijk Deskundigen (NRGD), governed by the College gerechtelijk deskundigen, is responsible for the following tasks:* deciding on an application for (re)registration in the NRGD, under articles 12 to 14 inclusive and 17 to 19 inclusive of the Besluit register deskundige in strafzaken (Brdis);* deciding on an application for (re)registration in, or on a possible removal from, the NRGD, under article 18 Brdis;* setting up and maintaining the register in which the above decisions are recorded, as well as giving instructions about it to the Bureau NRGD;* promoting the drafting of specific requirements per field of expertise, to further elaborate the requirements referred to in article 12, second paragraph, Brdis;* adopting a code of conduct containing the rules of conduct that registered experts must follow;* determining, in consultation with the secretary, the activities of the Bureau NRGD, in support of the work of the College gerechtelijk deskundigen.

Statutory task: * Providing subsidies that fully or partly cover the financial consequences of (among other things) the (partial) closure of care institutions, and supervising the restructuring;* deciding that approval is required for renting out, disposing of or encumbering with any limited right buildings or parts of buildings that will permanently no longer be used for the care institution. In doing so, deciding on the deposit of the book result into the Algemeen Fonds Bijzondere Ziektekosten;* providing subsidies when the location of a central post for ambulance transport is changed or closed, as well as restructuring ambulance transport where a licence has been withdrawn;* carrying out special assignments at the request of the Minister van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport.

As an independent authority, the CBG regulates the quality, efficacy and safety of a medicine, and the CBG promotes its proper use by the right patient. Our organisation consists of an agency ('the aCBG') and an independent administrative body ('the College'). The agency is responsible for preparing and implementing decisions of the College. On the basis of that preparatory assessment, the College gives an independent and expert judgement. The agency is also responsible for pharmacovigilance in the Netherlands and for receiving reports of medicine shortages. And the Dutch representatives on the committees of the European medicines agency EMA work at the agency. In addition to assessing medicines for humans, the agency also assesses veterinary medicines and novel foods. Final responsibility for assessing these lies with the ministerie van LVVN (veterinary medicines) and the ministerie van VWS (novel foods).

Statutory task: The College ter Beoordeling van Geneesmiddelen is responsible for authorising medicines, decides on the dispensing status and is charged with pharmacovigilance in the Netherlands, all in accordance with rules given by or under European directives and the Geneesmiddelenwet.

This is a cluster made up of independent administrative bodies that do not fall under the Kaderwet zelfstandige bestuursorganen. The underlying units of this cluster are therefore not named in the Register van Overheidsorganisaties.

The College van Toezicht Auteursrechten (CvTA) supervises the collective management organisations for copyright and neighbouring rights.

Statutory task: The main task of the College van Toezicht Auteursrechten (CVtA) is to supervise collective management organisations. These organisations have been designated by the minister of Justitie en Veiligheid to collect and distribute fees under the authority of the Auteurswet or the Wet op de Naburige Rechten.

The College voor de Rechten van de Mens was set up to see that human rights are properly protected and to inform people about this, in the Netherlands and Caribisch Nederland. As part of this mission, the College conducts research and advises the government and parliament. It also reports on human rights issues to international organisations, such as the UN. The College also rules on individual discrimination complaints and provides information, because it is important that people know what their rights are.

Statutory task: The College voor de Rechten van de Mens carries out the following tasks:* investigating possible (systematic) violations of human rights or the level of protection of these rights in a specific area;* conducting research into the protection of human rights;* investigating possible distinctions that exist or are made, as referred to in the Algemene wet gelijke behandeling, the Wet gelijke behandeling van mannen en vrouwen and article 646 of Boek 7 of the Burgerlijk Wetboek;* investigating possible systematic distinctions, as described above;* reporting on and ruling on the outcomes of the above investigations;* reporting on and making recommendations in the field of human rights, including reporting annually on the human rights situation in the Netherlands;* advising on (draft) legislation, regulations and policy that directly or indirectly relate to human rights;* providing information in the field of human rights and stimulating and coordinating education on human rights;* stimulating research into the protection of human rights;* cooperating structurally with civil society organisations and national, European and worldwide institutions, among other things by organising activities in cooperation with civil society organisations;* urging the ratification, implementation and observance of treaties on human rights and urging the withdrawal of reservations to such treaties;* urging the implementation and observance of binding decisions of international law organisations on human rights;* urging the observance of European or international recommendations on human rights;The mandate of the College also covers Caribisch Nederland (the islands of Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba). This applies to all tasks of the College, except the ruling task in the field of equal treatment.

The College voor de toelating van gewasbeschermingsmiddelen en biociden (Ctgb) is responsible for carrying out the Wet gewasbeschermingsmiddelen en biociden (Wgb).

Statutory task: The College voor de toelating van gewasbeschermingsmiddelen en biociden decides on the authorisation of plant protection products and biocides in the Netherlands.

Diplomas in the Netherlands are largely based on national, central exams. The trust that further education and employers place in diplomas depends on the quality of those exams. As the College voor Toetsen en Examens (CvTE), we provide exams that are worthy of that trust. We do this for the sectors primary education (po), secondary vocational education (mbo), secondary education (vo), state exams vo and the state exam Dutch as a second language (Nt2). In this we work closely with people from education.

Statutory task: The College voor Toetsen en Examens (CvTE) is responsible for, among other things:* setting and organising the central exams in regular secondary education;* setting and organising the central exams in Dutch language and English in mbo; * setting, organising and administering the state exams in secondary education;* setting, organising and administering the state exam Dutch as a second language;* organising and recognising the transfer tests and the tests of a pupil monitoring system.

The Commissariaat voor de Media is the regulator that checks whether the Mediawet 2008 and the Wet op de vaste boekenprijs are complied with. In this way, the Commissariaat ensures that everyone in the Netherlands has access to an independent and varied media offering. The Commissariaat also monitors whether all new books in Dutch or Frisian and all music publications are available at a fixed price.

Statutory task: The main tasks of the Commissariaat voor de Media are:* supervising compliance with the Mediawet 2008;* supervising compliance with the Wet op de vaste boekenprijs;* granting licences to commercial, regional and local public broadcasters;* supervising compliance with advertising and sponsorship rules, programme requirements, format obligations and programme quota requirements;* supervising the financial accountability of public broadcasters at national, regional and local level;* periodically advising on, among other things, the multi-year budgets of the public broadcaster and the concession policy plan;* supervising compliance with the Governancecode Publieke Omroep;* exercising meta-supervision of the [Nederlands Instituut voor de Classificatie van Audiovisuele Media (NICAM)](https://www.nicam.nl/);* publishing the Mediamonitor annually, which highlights the state of affairs in the Dutch media market.

The Commissie Eindtermen Accountantsopleiding (CEA) is an independent administrative body without legal personality; it sets the final attainment levels for accountancy education and supervises them. The legal basis for the CEA is found in articles 49 to 53 inclusive of the Wet op het Accountantsberoep (Wab). The committee consists of seven members. The Minister van Financiën appoints both the chair and the other members in a personal capacity and for a period of five years. The work of the committee is supported by the staff of its office.

This zbo is part of the cluster Registratiecommissies KNMG, KNMP, KNMT, FGzPt and V&VN. It is the registration committee of the Federatie van Gezondheidspsychologen en Psychotherapeuten (FGzPt). De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) is the central bank, supervisor and resolution authority that works for financial stability and sustainable prosperity in the Netherlands. In this way, DNB, together with European partners, contributes to price stability and balanced macroeconomic development in Europe, a shock-resistant financial system, secure and reliable payments, and sound financial institutions that meet their obligations and commitments. To strengthen the policy aimed at these objectives, DNB regularly issues independent economic advice. DNB is also responsible for payments in Caribisch Nederland. DNB also works with the Depositogarantiefonds to implement the deposit guarantee scheme in Caribisch Nederland. Together with the Autoriteit Financiële Markten (AFM), DNB supervises financial institutions located in Caribisch Nederland.

Statutory task: As an independent administrative body (zbo), De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) has the following tasks under article 4 of the Bankwet 1998:* supervising financial institutions under the applicable statutory rules;* promoting the smooth operation of payments;* promoting the stability of the financial system;* collecting statistical data and producing statistics under the applicable statutory rules;* carrying out resolution tasks relating to certain financial undertakings in accordance with the applicable statutory rules. DNB can, after permission by Koninklijk Besluit, also carry out tasks in the general interest other than those named in the Bankwet 1998. In addition to its zbo tasks set out in article 4 of the Bankwet 1998, DNB has the monetary tasks included in article 3 of the Bankwet 1998. Thus DNB is the central bank of the Netherlands and in that capacity (as a participant in the European System of Central Banks) is charged with tasks to implement the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. As central bank, DNB is fully independent of the minister of Financiën. Finally, DNB is responsible for payments in Caribisch Nederland. DNB works with both the Depositogarantiefonds and the Autoriteit Financiële Markten (AFM), respectively to implement the deposit guarantee scheme in Caribisch Nederland and to supervise financial institutions in Caribisch Nederland.

Statutory task: The tasks of the Landelijke commissie sociale hygiëne (Lcsh) are:* keeping the Register Sociale Hygiëne;* registering persons in the Register;* making the Register available for consultation;* reconfirming registrations from the old Register (before 1 July 2023 this was kept by the Landelijke Examencommissie of the Stichting Vakbekwaamheid Horeca);* recognising Sociale Hygiëne diplomas.

LVNL is responsible for managing civil airspace and everything that goes with it. We have done this since 1923, and since 1993 as a Zelfstandig Bestuursorgaan (ZBO).The statutory tasks of LVNL are set out in the Wet luchtvaart. They include:- Providing air traffic services within the Amsterdam flight information region.- Providing communication, navigation and surveillance services.- Providing aeronautical information services and issuing aeronautical publications and charts.- Providing or arranging training for air traffic safety and providing air navigation services.- Advising the minister of Infrastructuur en Waterstaat and the minister of Defensie on matters in the field of air traffic safety and the provision of air navigation services.- Performing other tasks assigned by or under the Wet luchtvaart.

Statutory task: * Handling air traffic safely and efficiently at and around the airports Amsterdam Airport Schiphol, Rotterdam Airport, Groningen Airport Eelde and Maastricht Aachen Airport and above the Netherlands up to 24,500 feet;* renewing and managing technical systems; * providing aeronautical information; * providing training for air traffic control; * providing aeronautical charts and publications.

As of 2010 there are 27 medical research ethics committees (METC's) recognised by the Centrale Commissie Mensgebonden Onderzoek (CCMO). For an overview, see the CCMO [website](https://www.ccmo.nl/).This is a cluster consisting of zelfstandige bestuursorganen that do not fall under the Kaderwet zelfstandige bestuursorganen. The underlying units of this cluster are therefore not named in the Register van Overheidsorganisaties.

Statutory task: Reviewing research protocols in accordance with the provisions of or under the law.

This is a cluster consisting of zelfstandige bestuursorganen that do not fall under the Kaderwet zelfstandige bestuursorganen. The underlying units of this cluster are therefore not named in the Register van Overheidsorganisaties.

The Mondriaan Fonds arose from the merger on 30 December 2011 of the Fonds BKVB, which focused on contemporary artists and intermediaries, and the Mondriaan Stichting, which focused on institutions in the field of visual art and cultural heritage.

Statutory task: The Mondriaan Fonds is the public fund for the promotion of visual art and cultural heritage. It promotes exceptional and innovative projects and activities of visual artists, intermediaries and institutions that are important for visual art and cultural heritage in the Netherlands. All financial contributions the Mondriaan Fonds provides aim to stimulate the meaningful development and visibility of visual art and cultural heritage in the Netherlands where the market does not, or does not yet, make this possible.

The Nationaal Rapporteur Mensenhandel en Seksueel Geweld tegen Kinderen is independent and has the statutory task of researching the nature and extent of human trafficking and sexual violence against children. It also has the statutory task of researching the effects of current policy on tackling human trafficking and sexual violence against children, and of advising the government on preventing and combating them.The Netherlands has had a Nationaal Rapporteur working on human trafficking since 2000. In 2009 the mandate was extended to tackling child pornography. In the first report on this mandate in 2011, the Nationaal Rapporteur concluded that tackling child pornography should be seen more broadly, in the context of sexual violence against children. The Dutch government then adopted this recommendation, which led in 2012 to the mandate being extended to sexual violence against children.The Nationaal Rapporteur is supported in their work by a bureau. Together with the bureau, the Nationaal Rapporteur forms the institute Nationaal Rapporteur Mensenhandel en Seksueel Geweld tegen Kinderen; the institute functions as a zelfstandig bestuursorgaan.

Statutory task: * researching the nature and extent of human trafficking and sexual violence against children;* researching the effects of policy intended to counter human trafficking and sexual violence against children;* advising national and local government and organisations in care services and criminal law on combating human trafficking and sexual violence against children;* sharing insights into the issue with members of the Tweede Kamer and municipalities.

Before 2017 this zbo was called Stichting Nationale en Internationale Wegvervoer Organisatie. Because of the change from private law (Stichting) to public law, it is now Nationale en Internationale Wegvervoer Organisatie (NIWO).

Statutory task: Promoting Dutch domestic and cross-border professional road haulage by: * (pursuant to article 32 wgw) granting and withdrawing licences for domestic professional transport as referred to in article 8 and article 12, first paragraph, respectively;* granting and withdrawing Community licences as referred to in article 10, second and fourth paragraph, respectively;* granting and withdrawing authorisations to carry out cross-border transport as referred to in article 25, first paragraph;* issuing additional documents for cross-border professional transport as referred to in article 26, first paragraph and second paragraph, part c, respectively;* other work to be assigned by or under an algemene maatregel van bestuur, relating to both domestic and cross-border professional transport;* (pursuant to article 7 Besluit goederenvervoer over de weg) keeping a registration and alert system to implement the provisions of article 12 of the law;* managing data files for its public tasks;* taking part in negotiations under bilateral treaties with other states, or to conclude bilateral treaties;* the NIWO can be given other tasks by ministerial regulation, which in any case include the implementation of Regulation (EEC) number 391/90.

The Nederlands Instituut Publieke Veiligheid (NIPV) is a knowledge institute that focuses on, among other things, crisis management and fire services. Through research, education, information provision and support, the NIPV strengthens various crisis partners, including the veiligheidsregio's and central government.

Statutory task: The Nederlands Instituut Publieke Veiligheid (NIPV) has the following tasks:* providing officer training, as well as providing other training courses (to be designated by the minister of Justitie en Veiligheid) that end with an exam as referred to in article 18, paragraph 4 of the Wet veiligheidsregio's;* developing teaching, exercise and learning material for the above training courses;* developing and maintaining expertise, by collecting and managing relevant knowledge and, where necessary, by carrying out applied scientific research;* making the collected information and expertise available to organisations working in fire services, disaster control, crisis management and medical assistance;* acquiring and managing equipment (including gear and telecommunication facilities) and, where necessary, making it available to the veiligheidsregio's and municipalities with a municipal fire service;* carrying out other work in fire services, disaster control, crisis management and medical assistance, as regards providing training other than that referred to above and developing teaching, exercise and learning material for such training;* recruiting and selecting candidates for the above training courses;* organising exercises;* carrying out other activities that promote the expertise of persons within fire services, disaster control, crisis management and medical assistance (or the functioning of the organisations they work for);* carrying out research for, and advising, third parties in order to contribute directly or indirectly to physical safety.

The Nederlands-Vlaamse Accreditatieorganisatie (NVAO) is responsible for accrediting existing and new programmes in higher education in Nederland and Vlaanderen. The NVAO also assesses the quality assurance of higher education institutions in Nederland and Vlaanderen, so that their quality is safeguarded in an expert and independent way.

Statutory task: The main tasks of the Nederlands-Vlaamse Accreditatieorganisatie (NVAO) are: * assessing and safeguarding the level and quality of higher education in Nederland and Vlaanderen; * promoting a culture of quality within higher education. The NVAO carries out these tasks from an international perspective and in the context of the European Bologna Process.

Statutory task: The registered pilots together form the Nederlandse loodsencorporatie (NLC). Membership of the corporation is compulsory and arises by operation of law. The NLC is a public professional body within the meaning of article 134 of the Grondwet. The corporation has regulatory powers over its members in a number of areas, such as training, professional practice and service provision. The regulations are enforced through disciplinary law, by the tuchtcollege loodsen. The corporation has three bodies: the chair, who represents the corporation externally, the general council, which forms the executive board, and the members' meeting, which adopts the regulations.

The Kaderwet zbo's does not apply because the body exercises no public authority (Tweede Kamer 2007-2008, 25268, number 50, statement by the minister of Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap).

Statutory task: TNO is an independent research organisation that, on the basis of its expertise and research, makes an important contribution to the competitiveness of companies and organisations, to the economy and to the quality of society as a whole.

The Nederlandse Organisatie voor Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek (NWO) ensures quality and innovation in science and is one of the most important funders of science in Nederland. Each year NWO invests almost 1 billion euros in curiosity-driven research, research aimed at societal challenges and research infrastructure. NWO selects and funds research proposals on the basis of advice from expert scientists and specialists from Nederland and abroad. NWO also has nine research institutes of its own, where internationally leading research is carried out. NWO stimulates national and international cooperation, invests in large research facilities and promotes the use of knowledge. NWO funds just over 7.000 research projects at universities and other knowledge institutions. NWO is an independent administrative body (zelfstandig bestuursorgaan) with tasks laid down by law. The organisation falls under the responsibility of the ministerie van Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap. The executive board bears final responsibility for carrying out the tasks of the whole umbrella organisation. The supervisory board advises the executive board (RvB) on request or on its own initiative and has an audit committee that advises the executive board on the budget, the annual accounts and the annual report. The advisory council can advise the executive board, on request or on its own initiative, on developments in society and science that are relevant to NWO. Domain boards, research institutes and coordinating bodies (temporary steering bodies) fall under the executive board. The quality, care and transparency of the assessment process and project management are important to NWO. The governance of NWO is laid down in the NWO-wet and regulations. For reasons of good governance, quality, care and transparency, the NWO subsidy regulation and a number of internal regulations have been adopted. The NWO domains, research institutes and coordinating bodies carry out NWO's core task: promoting quality and innovation in science. The NWO domains organise the programmes and funding for research. Both the executive board and the NWO domain boards have the power to distribute public funds for scientific research. Research is carried out at the NWO institutes. Coordinating bodies are temporary units with special attention for one, often multidisciplinary, field of research.

Statutory task: NWO's task is to promote the quality of scientific research and to initiate and stimulate new developments in scientific research. NWO carries out its task in particular by allocating resources. The organisation promotes the transfer of knowledge of the results of research it has initiated and stimulated, for the benefit of society. In carrying out its task, NWO focuses mainly on university research. In doing so it pays attention to coordination and promotes it where necessary.

The Nederlandse Publieke Omroep (NPO) is the steering and cooperation body responsible for carrying out the public media tasks at national level, as laid down in the Mediawet 2008.

Statutory task: The main tasks of the Nederlandse Publieke Omroep (NPO) are:* promoting cooperation and coordination within the national public broadcasting system;* allocating the airtime of institutions that have obtained national public airtime;* funding the institutions that have obtained national public airtime.

The Nederlandse Transplantatie Stichting (NTS) works to improve organ and tissue donation and transplantation. It supports the donor hospitals and transplant centres in Nederland. Since the introduction of the Wet op de orgaandonatie in 1997, the NTS has had the task of guiding donation and transplantation properly. It does this on behalf of the ministerie van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport (VWS).

Statutory task: The Nederlandse Transplantatie Stichting (NTS) has the following tasks and powers under the Wet op de orgaandonatie:* mediating in obtaining donor organs;* mediating in typing donor organs;* mediating in transporting donor organs;* allocating donor organs to a suitable recipient.

Statutory task: The Nederlandse Zorgautoriteit (NZa) is charged with:* market supervision, market development and tariff and performance regulation in the field of health care;* supervising the lawful implementation by health insurers of what is regulated by or under the Zorgverzekeringswet; * supervising the lawful settlement of the contributions referred to in articles 32 to 34 of the Zorgverzekeringswet, after an insurer has stopped providing health insurance; * supervising the lawful and effective implementation by the AWBZ insurers and the legal entities referred to in article 40 of the Algemene Wet Bijzondere Ziektekosten of what is regulated by or under that act and articles 91, second paragraph, second sentence, 123 and 124 of the Wet financiering sociale verzekeringen; * supervising the implementation of articles 41, 42 and 43 of the Wet marktordening gezondheidszorg. Article 3 of this act lays down the legal basis of the NZa. The NZa focuses, besides the funding of care providers and monitoring the proper implementation of insurance laws in health care, on proactively setting conditions for market forces and enforcing them. The aim of the new health care system is that consumers get value for their money. Efficiency, choice, quality and accessibility of care markets are central to this.

This is a cluster made up of independent administrative bodies that do not fall under the Kaderwet zelfstandige bestuursorganen. The underlying units of this cluster are therefore not named in the Register van Overheidsorganisaties.

Statutory task: * The law has given the notary the power to draw up authentic deeds, in particular in the fields of: - the law of persons and family law (drawing up marriage settlements, wills, divorce deeds, declarations of inheritance, etc.); - real property law (drawing up deeds of transfer, mortgage deeds, deeds in connection with a public auction, etc.); - the law of legal entities (drawing up deeds of incorporation, amendments to articles of association, deeds of transfer and issue (emission) of shares, deeds of legal merger and demerger and the like).* In addition, parties can also ask the notary to draw up other deeds for them in notarial form.

Nuffic helps schools and educational institutions in Nederland and abroad to make international education and cooperation possible. In addition, Nuffic is responsible in Nederland for the work of the Nationaal Agentschap Erasmus+ Onderwijs & Training.

Statutory task: Nuffic is the organisation in Nederland that deals with the internationalisation of education. As a zbo, Nuffic is responsible for carrying out the tasks of the Nationaal Agentschap Erasmus+ Onderwijs & Training.

This is a cluster made up of independent administrative bodies that do not fall under the Kaderwet zelfstandige bestuursorganen. The underlying units of this cluster are therefore not named in the Register van Overheidsorganisaties.

The Onderzoeksraad voor Veiligheid (OVV) investigates accidents and disasters in Nederland, with the aim of preventing them from happening again. As of 1 February 2005 the OVV is the continuation of the former Raad voor de Transportveiligheid.

Statutory task: The Onderzoeksraad voor Veiligheid (OVV) has the task, with the sole aim of preventing future incidents or limiting their consequences, of investigating and establishing the causes or probable causes of individual incidents or categories of incidents and the extent of their consequences, and where necessary of making recommendations to improve safety. The OVV is authorised to investigate events in fields such as traffic and transport, defence, health, the environment, industry, construction and nature. For example, the OVV can investigate fires, explosions or natural disasters, but in principle all incidents are eligible for investigation. The only exceptions are incidents in the field of public order, counter-terrorism, peace missions, acts of war and the like. The OVV has jurisdiction for the whole Koninkrijk, so for Nederland, Aruba, Curaçao and Sint Maarten.

ONVZ Langdurige Zorg B.V. is an implementing body of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz), as referred to in article 4.1.1 of that act.

Statutory task: ONVZ Langdurige Zorg B.V. is responsible for carrying out the tasks described in section 2 of chapter 4 (articles 4.2.1 to 4.2.6) of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz).

Statutory task: * Issuing decisions on an application for recognition, an extraordinary pension, a guarantee supplement, a (periodic) benefit, a guarantee benefit, compensation, an allowance or a review as referred to in the laws for resistance participants and war victims, made by a person who does not yet derive or has not derived a financial entitlement from the law on which the application is based; * Reviewing, on its own initiative, recognition as a resistance participant, persecuted person or civilian victim; * Setting policy rules for decisions of the Sociale Verzekeringsbank as referred to in article 6 (parts a, b and d); * Advising the Sociale Verzekeringsbank on decisions that cannot be taken on the basis of the policy rules referred to in part c.

Statutory task: * Supporting national recruitment and carrying out selection;* providing initial and post-initial police education (including examinations);* transferring knowledge to the Nederlandse politie and contributing to the development of the performance of the police task, among other things by carrying out research;* developing and providing training other than initial or post-initial education;* In addition, the Politieacademie may carry out market activities (see article 3 paragraph 2 of the Wet op het LSOP), provided that this work is related to the tasks above, does not lead to distortion of competition with private providers of comparable services and is carried out at prices that at least cover costs.

Accreditation is the assessment of whether a testing body, certification body, inspection body or laboratory (conformity assessment bodies) carries out its work impartially and competently. After a positive assessment, the accreditation body issues a formal statement that the body meets the requirements set by European harmonised standards (Staatscourant 2010, 3033) and, where applicable, by additional requirements.

Statutory task: * Carrying out the tasks assigned in regulation (EC) number 765/2008 (on accreditation and market surveillance). This includes assessing the competence of conformity assessment bodies to carry out a specific conformity assessment activity, * monitoring the conformity assessment bodies that have been granted an accreditation certificate * and the work in the context of peer evaluation.

As of 1 February 2006 the Raad voor het kwekersrecht, the Commissie voor de samenstelling van rassenlijst voor landbouwgewassen, the Commissie voor de samenstelling van rassenlijst voor bosbouwgewassen and the Commissie Toelating groenterassen were merged into the Raad voor plantenrassen. Since 1 January 2008 the Raad voor plantenrassen has been supported by the Bureau Administratie en Documentatie of Naktuinbouw, Rassen & Proeven department.

Statutory task: The Raad voor plantenrassen is responsible for:* granting plant breeders' rights;* admitting agricultural varieties;* admitting varieties and stands of forestry crops;* admitting vegetable varieties by means of the so-called B-list. The Raad also holds the Nederlands Rassenregister.

The Raad voor Rechtsbijstand (RvR) is, as an independent administrative body, responsible for providing subsidised legal aid in European Nederland and on Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba. In addition, the RvR implements (part of) the Wet schuldsanering natuurlijke personen (Wsnp) and the Wet beëdigde tolken en vertalers (Wbtv).

Statutory task: The Raad voor Rechtsbijstand (RvR) organises and provides legal aid and mediation, and supervises their delivery. The RvR also coordinates, on behalf of the Minister van Justitie en Veiligheid, the implementation of the Wet schuldsanering natuurlijke personen (Wsnp) and also implements the Wet beëdigde tolken en vertalers (Wbtv).

The RDW (formerly the Rijksdienst voor het Wegverkeer) is a public service provider in the mobility chain. As an independent administrative body, the RDW carries out a number of statutory and assigned tasks in the fields of admission of vehicles and their parts, supervision, enforcement, registration, provision of information and issuing documents. The RDW carries out these tasks in close cooperation with various partners in the mobility chain.

Statutory task: The RDW has four main assignments from the Dutch government:* admission: admitting vehicles and vehicle parts to the Dutch and European market;* supervision and inspection: supervising companies recognised by the RDW and inspecting the technical condition of vehicles;* registration and provision of information: collecting, storing, processing and managing data on vehicles, their owners and vehicle documents, and providing information on this data to interested parties;* issuing documents: issuing documents needed for vehicles or owners, such as registration certificates, driving licences and the APK form.

This cluster comprises the regional pilots' corporations (rlc's) Amsterdam-IJmond, Noord, Rotterdam-Rijnmond and Scheldemonden.

Statutory task: In addition, every registered pilot is by operation of law a member of one (or more) regional pilots' corporations (rlc's). The rlc's have a power, albeit a very limited one, to set additional rules for their members. Otherwise, the Nederlandse Loodsencorporatie and the rlc's provide training, examinations and information.

This zbo is part of the cluster Registratiecommissies KNMG, KNMP, KNMT, FGzPt en V&VN. It concerns the registration committee of the professional organisation Koninklijke Nederlandsche Maatschappij tot bevordering der Geneeskunst (KNMG). The Registratiecommissie Geneeskundig Specialisten (RGS), a body within the KNMG, periodically checks whether medical specialists meet the rules of the College Geneeskundige Specialismen. Doctors who meet these rules can register in a specialist register. The RGS was formed on 1 January 2013 from a merger of three registration committees: the Huisarts, Verpleeghuisarts en arts voor verstandelijk gehandicapten Registratie Commissie (HVRC), the Medisch Specialisten Registratie Commissie (MSRC) and the Sociaal-Geneeskundigen Registratie Commissie (SGRC).

Statutory task: If an organisation of practitioners of a profession as referred to in article 3 of the Wet beroepen in de individuele gezondheidszorg (Wet BIG) has a specialist register for registering practitioners who have acquired special expertise in practising a sub-area of their profession, and a title is attached to it, the Minister van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport may determine that this title is designated as a legally recognised specialist title. An application for this is made by the board of the organisation; the board may delegate this power to a body. This power may be delegated to the body (college) as referred to in article 14, second paragraph, sub d of the Wet BIG. The Registratiecommissie Geneeskundig Specialisten (RGS), as a body within the Koninklijke Nederlandsche Maatschappij tot bevordering der Geneeskunst (KNMG), is responsible for various tasks relating to the registers of medical specialists. These tasks are:* registering medical specialists in a specialist register;* periodically renewing the registrations mentioned above;* removing the registrations mentioned above.

This zbo is part of the cluster Registratiecommissies KNMG, KNMP, KNMT, FGzPt en V&VN. It concerns the registration committee of the professional organisation Verpleegkundigen en Verzorgenden Nederland (V&VN). The Registratiecommissie Specialismen Verpleegkunde (RSV), an independent body within V&VN, is responsible for the registration and re-registration of nurse specialists, on the basis of article 14 of the Wet op de beroepen in de individuele gezondheidszorg (Wet BIG). Designating the specialisms within nursing, setting up registers and drawing up the general rules on this is done by the College Specialismen Verpleegkunde (CSV). The RSV operates the registers and translates the rules of the CSV into practical implementation.

Statutory task: If an organisation of practitioners of a profession as referred to in article 3 of the Wet beroepen in de individuele gezondheidszorg (Wet BIG) has a specialist register for registering practitioners who have acquired special expertise in practising a sub-area of their profession, and a title is attached to it, the Minister van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport may determine that this title is designated as a legally recognised specialist title. An application for this is made by the board of the organisation; the board may delegate this power to a body. This power may be delegated to the body (college) as referred to in article 14, second paragraph, sub d of the Wet BIG. The Registratiecommissie Specialismen Verpleegkunde (RSV), as an independent body within Verpleegkundigen & Verzorgenden Nederland (V&VN), is responsible for various tasks relating to the registers of specialist nurses. These tasks are:* setting up and closing the training registers for nurses training to become specialists;* registering nurse specialists in training in the training registers;* recognising training institutions and practice institutions, head trainers and practice trainers;* supervising compliance with college decisions by trainers and training institutions (among other things through visitation);* setting up and closing the registers for nurse specialists;* registering and re-registering nurse specialists in the specialist registers for Algemene Gezondheidszorg (AGZ) and Geestelijke Gezondheidszorg (GGZ).

This zbo is part of the cluster Registratiecommissies KNMG, KNMP, KNMT, FGzPt en V&VN. It concerns the registration committee of the professional organisation Koninklijke Nederlandse Maatschappij tot bevordering der Tandheelkunde (KNMT). The Registratiecommissie Tandheelkundige Specialismen (RTS), an independent body within the KNMT, is charged with implementing and supervising the rules of the College Tandheelkundige Specialismen (CTS). The CTS rules relate among other things to the training programmes, trainers and training institutions for dental specialists, as well as the requirements for (re-)registration.

Statutory task: If an organisation of practitioners of a profession as referred to in article 3 of the Wet beroepen in de individuele gezondheidszorg (Wet BIG) has a specialist register for registering practitioners who have acquired special expertise in practising a sub-area of their profession, and a title is attached to it, the Minister van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport may determine that this title is designated as a legally recognised specialist title. An application for this is made by the board of the organisation; the board may delegate this power to a body. This power may be delegated to the body (college) as referred to in article 14, second paragraph, sub d of the Wet BIG. The Registratiecommissie Tandheelkundige Specialismen (RTS), as an independent body within the Koninklijke Nederlandse Maatschappij tot bevordering der Tandheelkunde (KNMT), is responsible for various tasks relating to the registers of dental specialists. These tasks include:* keeping a specialist register and a training register for the specialism Mondziekten, Kaak- en Aangezichtschirurgie (MKA);* keeping a specialist register and a training register for the specialism Dento-Maxillaire Orthopaedie (DMO);* supervising the rules of the College Tandheelkundige Specialismen (CTS);* implementing the rules of the CTS.

The professional organisations Koninklijke Nederlandsche Maatschappij tot bevordering der Geneeskunst (KNMG), Koninklijke Nederlandse Maatschappij ter bevordering der Pharmacie (KNMP), Koninklijke Nederlandse Maatschappij tot bevordering der Tandheelkunde (KNMT), Federatie van Gezondheidspsychologen en Psychotherapeuten (FGzPt) and Verpleegkundigen & Verzorgenden Nederland (V&VN) as a whole are not independent administrative bodies belonging to this cluster. The registration committees of these professional organisations are.

Statutory task: If an organisation of practitioners of a profession as referred to in article 3 of the Wet beroepen in de individuele gezondheidszorg (Wet BIG) mentioned above has a specialist register for registering practitioners who have acquired special expertise in practising a sub-area of their profession, and a title is attached to it, the Minister van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport may determine that this title is designated as a legally recognised specialist title. An application for this is made by the board of the organisation; the board may delegate this power to a body. This power may be delegated to the body (college) as referred to in article 14, second paragraph, sub d of the Wet BIG. In short: * registering specialists;* removing the registration of specialists;* suspending the registration of specialists.
