Statutory task: The Rijkshavenmeester/the Havenbedrijf Rotterdam carries out nautical management/tasks for the Gemeente Rotterdam and the central government, such as with regard to admission policy, imposing compulsory pilotage on an ad hoc basis, giving orders for fairway marking and giving traffic instructions.

Salland Zorgkantoor B.V. is an implementing body of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz), as referred to in article 4.1.1 of that act. This Wlz implementing body also has a care office function.

Statutory task: Salland Zorgkantoor B.V. is responsible for carrying out the tasks described in section 2 of chapter 4 (articles 4.2.1 to 4.2.6) of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz). As a care office, Salland Zorgkantoor B.V. also has a duty of care towards all insured persons living in the region for which Salland Zorgkantoor B.V. has been designated as care office. This duty of care includes providing a personal budget (pgb) and handling the administration or checking of the care provided to insured persons in the region concerned. The extent of that administration or checking is determined by an Algemene Maatregel van Bestuur.

Statutory task: * a. developing and maintaining a national qualification structure aimed at matching the supply of vocational education to the needs of society, partly in light of the labour market for graduates and partly with regard to relevant international developments, among other things by making proposals to the minister of OCW for the qualification files referred to in article 7.2.4, second paragraph,; * b. contributing to an efficient and targeted use of public funds by developing proposals on which vocational programmes qualify for funding from the national treasury; * c. promoting the quality of work-based learning; * d. developing and setting quality criteria for work-based learning places and assessing, at least once every four years, companies and organisations that provide work-based learning against these criteria, and publishing a list of companies and organisations that meet these criteria; * e. ensuring as far as possible the availability of a sufficient number of companies and organisations of adequate quality that provide work-based learning; * f. carrying out research in support of the tasks mentioned above, and; * g. carrying out additional activities to improve the match between education and the labour market;

Skal Biocontrole is the Dutch supervisor of the organic chain. The foundation certifies companies that carry out organic activities and checks whether the production, processing and trade of organic products complies with both Dutch and European rules.

Statutory task: Stichting Skal Biocontrole is designated as the competent authority for carrying out statutory tasks in the field of supervision, inspection and certification arising from the European regulations for a statutory organic quality mark.

The department Sociaal-economische en ruimtelijke statistieken (SER) of the CBS consists of the divisions below, each of which is divided into a number of teams:SBM (Policy and management support):* SIM (Information management)* SBS (Policy staff)SQS (Quaternary sector):* SGZ (Health and care)* SND (Education)* SRV (Legal protection and security)* SCT (Culture, tourism and technology)SLO (Living environment):* SRR (Region and space)* SVW (Real estate and housing market)* SLN (Agriculture and nature)* SMI (Environment)* SEN (Energy)SES (Demographic and socio-economic statistics):* SAM (Labour market)* SDE (Demography)* SOZ (Social security)* SET (Socio-economic overall picture)* CN (Caribisch Nederland)SAL (Labour, income and living conditions):* SPR (Production)* SDV (Dynamic processing)* SAD (Labour, dynamics and mobility)* SIL (Living conditions, income and cohesion)SVV (Traffic and transport):* SGV (Freight transport)* SGP (Passenger transport)The divisions and teams are taken from the [CBS-organogram](https://www.cbs.nl/-/media/_pdf/organogram-nl.pdf).

The Sociale Verzekeringsbank (SVB) has been implementing various schemes in social security and care for some 120 years. These are schemes for different groups of people such as older people, parents, surviving dependants, holders of a personal budget, resistance participants and war victims, and many others. We do this on behalf of governments and other bodies. Our main client is the Ministerie van Sociale Zaken en Werkgelegenheid. We also work for other clients, such as the ministerie van Volksgezondheid Welzijn en Sport.

Statutory task: The Sociale Verzekeringsbank (SVB) has the following tasks:* implementing the Algemene Ouderdomswet, the Algemene nabestaandenwet, the Algemene Kinderbijslagwet and laws governing the implementation of these laws;* ensuring that sound information is provided, on request or unsolicited, to employers, employees, benefit recipients, insured persons and other interested parties in connection with the implementation of the laws mentioned above;* carrying out tasks assigned to the SVB by laws other than those mentioned above;* managing and administering the funds referred to in article 1 Wet structuur uitvoeringsorganisatie werk en inkomen, parts f and g of the Wet financiering sociale verzekeringen and the Algemeen Kinderbijslagfonds, referred to in article 29a of the Algemene Kinderbijslagwet;* carrying out research into the statutory tasks of the SVB on behalf of the minister of Sociale Zaken en Werkgelegenheid (SZW) or on its own initiative;* providing the minister of SZW, at the minister's request, with the information needed to assess the feasibility of policy intentions and statutory rules;* keeping adequate records in order to carry out the tasks of the SVB;* providing services for data exchange with other countries and processing data from other countries;* at the request of an insured person, a health insurer or another interested party, providing information on the insurance status of the insured person (insofar as this information is necessary for implementing the Algemene Wet Bijzondere Ziektekosten and the Zorgverzekeringswet) and, at the request of an insured person, providing information on the insurance periods and the entitlement to old age pension based on them.

This zbo is part of the cluster Registratiecommissies KNMG, KNMP, KNMT, FGzPt en V&VN. The Specialisten Registratie Commissie (SRC) is the registration committee of the professional organisation Koninklijke Nederlandse Maatschappij ter bevordering der Pharmacie (KNMP). The registration committee is a part-time zbo set up under private law with public law tasks. The SRC was set up by the KNMP as supervisor of the quality of the training and the profession of pharmacist. The SRC consists of two chambers: one for community pharmacy (SRC-OF) and one for hospital pharmacy (SRC-ZF).

Statutory task: If an organisation of practitioners of a profession as referred to in article 3 of the Wet beroepen in de individuele gezondheidszorg (Wet BIG) has a specialist register for registering practitioners who have acquired special expertise in practising a sub-area of their profession, and a title is attached to it, the Minister van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport may determine that this title is designated as a legally recognised specialist title. An application for this is made by the board of the organisation; the board may delegate this power to a body. This power may be delegated to the body (college) as referred to in article 14, second paragraph, sub d of the Wet BIG. The Specialisten Registratie Commissie (SRC) was established by the Koninklijke Nederlandse Maatschappij ter bevordering der Pharmacie (KNMP) as supervisor of the quality of the training and the profession of the specialisms of community pharmacist and hospital pharmacist. The tasks of the SRC are:* opening or closing a register as referred to in article 11 under c or e of the Regeling Specialismen en profielen Farmacie 2023, after the Centraal College has decided to establish or withdraw it;* registering a pharmacist in a specialist register and removing the registration;* re-registering a pharmacist in a specialist register, whether or not directly following on, whether or not on the basis of equivalent activities, and removing the registration;* registering the pharmacist in a training register and amending or removing the registration;* issuing a training title if a pharmacist has successfully completed the specialist training in Nederland;* recognising professional qualifications;* recognising or renewing recognition of a trainer or training institution, and amending, suspending or withdrawing the recognition;* supervising compliance with a decision of the Centraal College by a trainer, training institution, training institute or pharmacist in training;* drawing up implementing regulations on the basis of decisions of the Centraal College, concerning training and/or re-registration and/or renewed registration in the specialist register; * supervising the specialist register.

Staatsbosbeheer, founded in 1899, is a legal entity with a statutory task (RWT): managing the land entrusted to it and making it sustainably useful to society.

Statutory task: Managing state forests and nature areas.

The Stichting Administratie Indonesische Pensioenen (SAIP) is an independent administrative body (zbo) under the ministerie van Binnenlandse Zaken (BZK). Its board is formed by a Raad van Beheer, which is charged with managing the foundation's funds and with granting, calculating, paying and administering the overseas pensions and benefits. Under the SAIP's articles of association, the Raad van Beheer accounts to the ministers of BZK and Financiën by means of the annual report. The SAIP has no staff of its own. Under an agreement concluded by the Raad van Beheer with the Stichting Pensioenfonds ABP, the implementation work lies with that pension fund. ABP has in turn assigned the implementation of this work to APG.

Statutory task: The Stichting Administratie Indonesische Pensioenen (SAIP) has the following tasks:* ensuring the fulfilment of the obligation to pay widows' pensions and orphans' allowances to the surviving relatives of former government staff of Indonesië;* taking decisions on behalf of the minister concerned to implement the schemes and matters relating to so-called overseas pensions and benefits.

The Autoriteit Financiële Markten (AFM) ensures that the financial markets operate transparently. The AFM's supervision focuses among other things on saving, investing, insurance, lending, pensions, capital markets, asset management, audit firms and financial reporting. The AFM also supervises financial undertakings in Caribisch Nederland, together with De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB).

Statutory task: The main task of the AFM is conduct supervision of the financial markets, to promote an orderly and transparent market process, fair relations between market parties and the protection of consumers. The AFM has this supervisory task under the Wet op het financieel toezicht (Wft). The AFM also decides on the admission of financial undertakings to the financial markets. The AFM supervises financial undertakings in Caribisch Nederland together with De Nederlandse Bank (DNB).

The Stichting Blik op Werk was founded as an independent quality institute and has been designated by the Regeling inburgering 2021 as the organisation that awards and manages the Keurmerk Inburgeren.

Statutory task: Blik op Werk grants a quality mark to organisations whose services promote sustainable labour participation and civic integration. The quality of the services provided by quality mark holders is independently checked. Blik op Werk also supports quality mark holders in making their services transparent, visible and findable in the Blik op Werk Kwaliteitsregister.

Since 1923, inspecting flower bulbs has been the core task of the foundation Bloembollenkeuringsdienst (BKD). We inspect for both quality and quarantine infestations. We carry out quality inspections, laboratory testing and import inspections. We also carry out export inspections on behalf of the Nederlandse Voedsel en Waren Autoriteit (NVWA). BKD supports market access by inspecting flower bulbs at a leading level of quality and provides (inter)national guarantees for the quality of flower bulbs. We carry out these inspections in an independent, reliable and efficient way and are therefore an important link in quality assurance for businesses and the flower bulb sector. The BKD is an independent administrative body and we carry out our statutory tasks on behalf of and under the supervision of the ministerie van Landbouw, Visserij, Voedselzekerheid en Natuur (LVVN).

Statutory task: The Bloembollenkeuringsdienst carries out phytosanitary and quality inspections of flower bulbs.

The Stichting Controle Orgaan Kwaliteits Zaken (COKZ) is the Dutch supervisor in the field of dairy, poultry and eggs. In carrying out this supervision, the COKZ implements Dutch and European rules. The COKZ is the successor of the Centraal Orgaan Zuivelcontrole (COZ) and the Centraal Orgaan Melkhygiëne (COM). The tasks of the Controlebureau voor Pluimvee, Eieren en Eiproducten (CPE) were also transferred to the COKZ as of 1 July 2012.

Statutory task: The Controle Orgaan Kwaliteits Zaken (COKZ) has, among others, the following tasks:* supervising compliance with process and product quality criteria in the dairy and egg sector;* safeguarding the safety and quality of milk, dairy products, eggs and egg products produced in Nederland;* keeping a register of approved companies (supervised by the COKZ) and making it available to the Nederlandse Voedsel- en Warenautoriteit (NVWA).

Our mission: Culture does something. It has a connecting, inspiring and stimulating power. The Fonds voor Cultuurparticipatie supports the cultural sector in achieving active participation in art and culture by as many Dutch people as possible, including those for whom taking part in culture is not a matter of course. The Fonds contributes to a resilient, agile and future-proof sector that can make full use of the thinking and making power of culture for our society. Active participation in culture brings people together, challenges them and offers new perspectives. Art and culture can increase opportunities and reduce differences, broaden views and enrich people. Culture helps you believe in yourself and put yourself in someone else's shoes, creates possibilities and lets you meet like-minded people and people who think differently. From Amsterdam to Appingedam and from Wilnis to Willemstad: culture belongs to every Dutch person. We believe in the positive impact of culture on every individual, with a strong, social and resilient society as a result. An assignment with impact: As a national culture fund, we stimulate active participation in culture in the Koninkrijk der Nederlanden. We do this by contributing to cultural education in and outside school, active cultural participation, accessibility of talent development, active heritage participation and international cooperation. How? To give as many people as possible access to art and culture, we work according to the following principles: Culture close by for everyone: We are committed to a solid cultural infrastructure everywhere in our Koninkrijk, so that culture is accessible to everyone and can be of value to society. We take into account the differences between regions and work with regional and local partners on (local) strengthening. Through them, as a national fund, we are close to our applicants and target groups, we contribute to future-proof ecosystems for art and culture and we can better drive cross-sector cooperation. Offering equal opportunities: In addition, it is of the utmost importance that our cultural policy is fair. This means that we make an extra effort to reach target groups for whom the distance to cultural participation is greater than for others, and that we focus on removing the factors that cause this inequality.

Statutory task: Providing and monitoring subsidies in the field of cultural participation.

Stichting Groene Erkenningen was formed on 1 January 2023 from a merger of the Bureau Erkenningen with Groenkeur. The zbo activities of the foundation continue to operate under the name Bureau Erkenningen. In 2023 the Stichting voor de Plaagdierbeheersing, the Stichting Examen- en Certificeringsinstituut Plaagdierpreventie and the Stichting Certificeringsinstituut Plaagdierbeheersing, Milieu en Volksgezondheid were dissolved. Their activities have been continued by Stichting Groene Erkenningen under the name Register Plaagdierbeheersing, Milieu en Veiligheid (RPMV). This activity is also a statutory task that the foundation carries out. The foundation has been appointed by the designated inspection bodies under the WAS2023, transitioning into the WAAS, to draw up and manage a scheme in close consultation with the ministerie van VWS. The private and public tasks are separate activities within the foundation. The foundation is an authority in independently making and managing standards that are self-evident and that demonstrate that work in the living environment is done competently, safely and responsibly.

Statutory task: Stichting Groene Erkenningen is responsible for issuing and recognising, on application, certificates of professional competence in the field of plant protection products and/or biocides.

Statutory task: * The main task of the KCB is inspecting fresh fruit and vegetables, cut flowers and potted plants. The KCB carries out: * import and export inspection (quality) of fresh fruit and vegetables; * quality control of fresh fruit and vegetables traded within Nederland, with the exception of the retail stage; * import inspection (phytosanitary) of fresh fruit and vegetables, cut flowers and potted plants and of plant products that do not fall under a specific sector, also called 'miscellaneous products'; * sampling and monitoring activities for export to specific destinations, including the 'Monitoring vruchtgroenten' intended for Japan, USA and Canada.; * In addition, the KCB carries out a number of projects for the government, such as Survey Tuta Absoluta in the final cultivation of tomato and Survey Afrikaanse fruitmot in the final cultivation of sweet pepper. The phytosanitary export inspection of plant products and the issuing of phytosanitary export certificates are carried out by NVWA officials.; * The endorsement of phytosanitary certificates with a CITES annotation is also carried out by NVWA officials. The KCB receives applications for phytosanitary export inspections and requests for the issue of phytosanitary export certificates.;
Statutory task: Milieukeur is responsible for issuing an EU ecolabel.

Statutory task: Stimulating film production in the Netherlands, with an emphasis on quality and diversity, and promoting a good climate for Dutch film culture. To achieve this, the Fonds gives filmmakers financial support in developing, making and distributing films. The Fonds is involved in the making of feature films, documentary films, experimental films, short films and animated films. In addition, the Fonds has money for special activities in the field of film.
Statutory task: Granting subsidies to artists and institutions for activities aimed at creating, producing, presenting and consuming performing arts.

The Nederlands Jeugdinstituut (NJi) is a national knowledge centre that works to give every child a promising youth. To reach that goal, the NJi collects knowledge about growing up and enriches, interprets and shares it. The NJi also helps apply the collected knowledge and manages the implementation of the part of the Erasmus programme that relates to youth, as laid down in the Uitvoeringsbesluit Uitvoeringswet Erasmusprogramma en programma Europees Solidariteitskorps VWS.

Statutory task: The Nederlands Jeugdinstituut (NJi) has the following tasks:* collecting current knowledge about how children grow up;* enriching, interpreting and sharing this knowledge;* drawing attention to the collected knowledge and helping to apply it;* managing the implementation of the Erasmus programme, where this relates to youth.

The Nederlands Letterenfonds was formed in 2010 from a merger of the Stichting Fonds voor de Letteren and the Stichting Nederlands Literair Productie- en Vertalingenfonds.

Statutory task: The main objective of the Nederlands Letterenfonds is to promote the following:* the quality and diversity of Dutch, Frisian and Papiamento language literature and the quality and diversity of literary works in Dutch Sign Language;* the quality and diversity of literature from other language areas in Dutch, Frisian or Papiamento translation or in translation into Dutch Sign Language;* the translation of high quality original Dutch, Frisian and Papiamento language literary works and literary works in Dutch Sign Language into languages other than Dutch, Frisian and Papiamento, as well as the international distribution of these translations and furthermore everything related to this or that may contribute to it.

The Nederlandse Algemene Keuringsdienst voor zaaizaad en pootgoed van landbouwgewassen carries out statutory inspections on behalf of and under the supervision of the ministerie van Landbouw, Natuur en Voedselkwaliteit. Among other things, potatoes, soil and seeds are assessed on various quality characteristics.

Statutory task: * Promoting, by means of inspections, that reliable propagating material of agricultural crops is placed on the market, traded further and exported;* issuing certificates as proof of approval;* supervising compliance with the regulations;* carrying out phytosanitary export and import inspections and authenticating the phytosanitary certificate.

The Stichting Nederlandse Algemene Kwaliteitsdienst Tuinbouw (Naktuinbouw) was formed on 1 January 2000 from a merger of the Stichting Nederlandse Algemene Keuringsdienst voor Bloemisterij en Boomkwekerijgewassen with the Stichting Nederlandse Algemene Keuringsdienst voor Groente- en Bloemzaden. Naktuinbouw examines propagating material (such as seeds, cuttings and young plants) and new plant varieties produced by horticultural businesses. In addition, Naktuinbouw inspects seed and plant material and tests it for diseases and pests.

Statutory task: * Promotes and safeguards the quality of products, processes and chains in horticulture focused on propagating material, both nationally and internationally. * Carrying out phytosanitary export and import inspections and authenticating the phytosanitary certificate.

Statutory task: Carrying out guardianship for unaccompanied minor asylum seekers and family guardianship for minor children who stay in a reception centre of the Centraal Orgaan opvang asielzoekers (COA).

Vervangingsfonds and Participatiefonds (VfPf) are two independent administrative bodies that are closely intertwined. We work from statutory tasks set out in the Wet op het primair onderwijs. VfPf is the HRM expert that advises and supports schools in their ambitions and development into future-proof and professional organisations.The best education for children comes about in well-functioning school organisations where everyone enjoys working and keeps doing so. VfPf advises and supports school boards in strengthening their responsibility to keep employees sustainably employable within the sector. So that absenteeism and unemployment are as low as possible. We do this with our expertise and experience from inside and outside the education field. We believe in sustainable solutions and always offer customised support, tailored to regional needs. Where necessary, VfPf absorbs the financial consequences of absenteeism and unemployment and quickly guides benefit recipients to a suitable new job. VfPf is of and for primary education and works on a not-for-profit basis. Together with school boards, we work on an attractive and vital sector.

Statutory task: Ensuring reimbursement of the costs related to unemployment benefits for education staff in primary and secondary education.

The Regionale Publieke Omroep (RPO) is a foundation established by the Mediawet that promotes cooperation between public broadcasters in different regions. In addition, the RPO acts as a coordinating body for these broadcasters.

Statutory task: The main tasks of the Regionale Publieke Omroep (RPO) are:* promoting cooperation between public broadcasters at regional level;* coordinating public broadcasters at regional level, with a view to carrying out their public media remit* looking after matters of common interest to the regional public media service and the regional public media institutions;* concluding collective labour agreements and setting payment standards for work supplied by freelancers, partly on behalf of the regional public media institutions;* promoting efficient use of money intended for producing and distributing media content, as well as promoting integrated financial reporting and accountability;* setting up, maintaining, managing, operating and regulating the use of bodies, services and facilities (such as studios and distribution infrastructures) needed for proper performance of the public media remit at regional level.

The Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie is the national cultural fund for design, architecture and digital culture. The task of the Stimuleringsfonds is, from a cultural perspective, to continue and renew the rich design tradition of the Netherlands by stimulating the process of experimenting, researching and making, and by promoting good commissioning.

Statutory task: The fund supports designers and makers with (inter)national projects, cultural institutions with one-year and multi-year programmes, and talents in the creative industry. Its core task is stimulating culture. An important theme is improving the chain between designers/makers and clients/producers. With programmes, events, publications and knowledge pooling, the fund also actively makes connections itself between culture, entrepreneurship and social engagement.

Vervangingsfonds and Participatiefonds (VfPf) are two independent administrative bodies that are closely intertwined. We work from statutory tasks set out in the Wet op het primair onderwijs. VfPf is the HRM expert that advises and supports schools in their ambitions and development into future-proof and professional organisations.The best education for children comes about in well-functioning school organisations where everyone enjoys working and keeps doing so.VfPf advises and supports school boards in strengthening their responsibility to keep employees sustainably employable within the sector. So that absenteeism and unemployment are as low as possible. We do this with our expertise and experience from inside and outside the education field.We believe in sustainable solutions and always offer customised support, tailored to regional needs.Where necessary, VfPf absorbs the financial consequences of absenteeism and unemployment and quickly guides benefit recipients to a suitable new job.VfPf is of and for primary education and works on a not-for-profit basis. Together with school boards, we work on an attractive and vital sector.

Statutory task: Ensuring reimbursement of the costs related to replacing staff of educational institutions in primary and secondary education.

In 2015 (on the basis of Woningwet art. 53a) the minister designated SVWN as the independent body that accredits visitation agencies. In addition, we develop and manage the visitation methodology and supervise the quality of visitations. SVWN also publishes all visitation reports.

Statutory task: * The independent body has the task of ensuring that a visitation can be carried out at housing corporations once every four years, specifically by designating 'expert bodies'. SVWN does this by accrediting agencies that may carry out visitations. (see also art. 2 of the Statuten).

Stichting Wlz-uitvoerder Zorg en Zekerheid is an implementing body of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz), as referred to in article 4.1.1 of that law. This Wlz implementing body also has a care office (zorgkantoor) function.

Statutory task: Stichting Wlz-uitvoerder Zorg en Zekerheid is responsible for carrying out the tasks described in section 2 of chapter 4 (articles 4.2.1 to 4.2.6 inclusive) of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz). As a care office, Stichting Wlz-uitvoerder Zorg en Zekerheid also has a duty of care towards all insured persons living in the region for which Stichting Wlz-uitvoerder Zorg en Zekerheid has been designated as care office. This duty of care includes, among other things, providing a personal budget (pgb) and handling the administration or checking of the care provided to insured persons in the region concerned. The extent of that administration or checking is determined by an Algemene Maatregel van Bestuur.

Stichting Zorgkantoor Menzis is an implementing body of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz), as referred to in article 4.1.1 of that law. This Wlz implementing body also has a care office (zorgkantoor) function.

Statutory task: Stichting Zorgkantoor Menzis is responsible for carrying out the tasks described in section 2 of chapter 4 (articles 4.2.1 to 4.2.6 inclusive) of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz). As a care office, Stichting Zorgkantoor Menzis also has a duty of care towards all insured persons living in the region for which Stichting Zorgkantoor Menzis has been designated as care office. This duty of care includes, among other things, providing a personal budget (pgb) and handling the administration or checking of the care provided to insured persons in the region concerned. The extent of that administration or checking is determined by an Algemene Maatregel van Bestuur.

The Stimuleringsfonds voor de Journalistiek stimulates the quality, diversity and independence of journalism by promoting the renewal of the journalistic infrastructure in the Netherlands with money, knowledge and research. It does this, among other things, through subsidy schemes, research and by organising events on innovation, investigative journalism and regional and local journalism. In addition, the Fonds shares the latest developments in the journalism sector via the news page on its website.As an independent administrative body (ZBO), the Stimuleringsfonds receives an annual contribution from the ministerie van Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap, from which all activities are funded.

Statutory task: The Stimuleringsfonds voor de Journalistiek (SvdJ) has the following tasks:* maintaining and promoting the pluriformity of the press, insofar as it matters for informing the public and forming opinion;* providing financial support to the press;* carrying out or commissioning research into the functioning of the press.

The Netherlands must be able to trust the quality of construction. That is what the Toelatingsorganisatie Kwaliteitsborging Bouw (TloKB) works on every day. The TloKB supervises quality assurance in construction, recognises the quality of construction products and registers certificates for work on gas combustion installations.As a public, independent party, the TloKB supervises the building quality system as a whole and enforces where necessary. It always does so carefully and transparently. With an eye for the public interest of building quality. Because that is what the TloKB stands for: better trust in the quality of construction.

Statutory task: The Toelatingsorganisatie Kwaliteitsborging Bouw (TloKB) carries out various subtasks in three main areas. These main areas are as follows:* quality assurance;* recognised quality declarations;* work on gas combustion installations.

This is a cluster of independent administrative bodies to which the Kaderwet zelfstandige bestuursorganen does not apply. It concerns health insurers admitted by the Nederlandse Zorgautoriteit as implementing bodies of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz), some of which also act as a care office (zorgkantoor).

Statutory task: Efficient and qualitatively sound implementation of the Wet langdurige zorg, in particular carrying out the duty of care for their own insured persons.

UWV is a vital part of society and works for everyone on the labour market. We work to prevent unemployment and incapacity for work. We do this by applying the human touch more often in our services. By further improving our services. By working together with our external partners.

VGZ Zorgkantoor B.V. is an implementing body of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz), as referred to in article 4.1.1 of that law. This Wlz implementing body also has a care office (zorgkantoor) function.

Statutory task: VGZ Zorgkantoor B.V. is responsible for carrying out the tasks described in section 2 of chapter 4 (articles 4.2.1 to 4.2.6 inclusive) of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz). As a care office, VGZ Zorgkantoor B.V. also has a duty of care towards all insured persons living in the region for which VGZ Zorgkantoor B.V. has been designated as care office. This duty of care includes, among other things, providing a personal budget (pgb) and handling the administration or checking of the care provided to insured persons in the region concerned. The extent of that administration or checking is determined by an Algemene Maatregel van Bestuur.

This is a cluster consisting of independent administrative bodies that do not fall under the Kaderwet zelfstandige bestuursorganen. The underlying parts of this cluster are therefore not named in the Register van Overheidsorganisaties.

This organisation is part of the Waarborginstellingen cluster.

Statutory task: Assaying submitted objects for their platinum, gold, palladium and silver content and hallmarking these articles.

This cluster comprises the assay offices Edelmetaal Waarborg Nederland B.V. (EWN) and WaarborgHolland B.V., which are responsible for assaying submitted articles for their platinum, gold, palladium and silver content, as well as hallmarking these articles.

Statutory task: Assaying submitted objects for their platinum, gold, palladium and silver content and hallmarking these articles.

The Waarderingskamer checks whether Dutch municipalities implement the Wet waardering onroerende zaken (Wet WOZ) correctly.

Statutory task: The main tasks of the Waarderingskamer are:* supervising the valuation and the determination of the value of real estate (with a view to taxation by the Rijk, the municipalities and the water boards) and the other subjects regulated in the Wet WOZ, so that various taxes can be levied equitably and efficiently;* advising the staatssecretaris van Financiën, on request or on its own initiative, on legislation, regulations and policy regarding the Wet WOZ, as well as developments in the field of the WOZ;* handling disputes between municipalities and other users of value data (such as the Rijk and the water boards) about the implementation of the Wet WOZ;* providing information to municipalities and other WOZ stakeholders.

Zilveren Kruis Zorgkantoor N.V. is an implementing body of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz), as referred to in article 4.1.1 of that law. This Wlz implementing body also has a care office (zorgkantoor) function.

Statutory task: Zilveren Kruis Zorgkantoor N.V. is responsible for carrying out the tasks described in section 2 of chapter 4 (articles 4.2.1 to 4.2.6 inclusive) of the Wet langdurige zorg (Wlz). As a care office, Zilveren Kruis Zorgkantoor N.V. also has a duty of care towards all insured persons living in the region for which Zilveren Kruis Zorgkantoor N.V. has been designated as care office. This duty of care includes, among other things, providing a personal budget (pgb) and handling the administration or checking of the care provided to insured persons in the region concerned. The extent of that administration or checking is determined by an Algemene Maatregel van Bestuur.

Zorginstituut Nederland took over the tasks of the College voor Zorgverzekeringen as of 1 April 2014. The College voor Zorgverzekeringen has been abolished.

Statutory task: Zorginstituut Nederland has the following tasks:* promoting the lawful and efficient implementation of the Wet Langdurige Zorg (Wlz) by the Wlz implementing bodies and the CAK; * promoting a uniform interpretation of the nature, content and scope of the insured package;* setting policy rules for the Wlz implementing bodies and for the CAK with a view to the lawful and efficient implementation of the Wlz;* informing Wlz implementing bodies, care providers and citizens about the nature, content and scope of the care that belongs to the insured package;* advising the minister van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport (VWS), on request, on intended policy regarding the nature, content and scope of the care that belongs to the insured package;* passing on to the minister van VWS, whether asked or not, factual developments that may give rise to changes in the nature, content and scope of the care that belongs to the insured package;* carrying out the activities named by or under an order in council for the joint care for maintaining electronic data exchange, as referred to in article 9.1.6, first paragraph, of the Wlz.

With all kinds of subsidy programmes we stimulate and fund knowledge development in the field of health, care and wellbeing. In addition, we stimulate the use of the knowledge developed and identify where knowledge is needed. In this way we keep responding to the changing world around us.We increase the relevance, quality and impact of knowledge and innovations and speed up practical applications in order to contribute to good health for everyone. As an organisation we support the entire knowledge chain: from fundamental research, to practice-oriented and action research, to implementation projects.Socially relevant themes are central within the organisation. These themes are carried out, in the form of programmes, within various clusters. Each cluster has its own team with a manager. The staff departments Beleid, Advies en Strategie (BAS) and Bedrijfsvoering support the organisation. The organisation as a whole is led by general director Véronique Timmerhuis. She works together with the management team, which consists of two programme directors, who direct the content clusters, and the heads of department of BAS and Bedrijfsvoering. The ZonMw board is the highest governing body of ZonMw.

Statutory task: ZonMw is an intermediary organisation that has projects, experiments, research and development in the field of health, prevention and care carried out in a programmatic way. ZonMW safeguards their quality, relevance and coherence. The activities cover the entire continuum from fundamental medical research up to and including application and implementation of research projects. The main commissioning parties are the ministerie van Volksgezondheid, Welzijn en Sport (VWS) and the Nederlandse Organisatie voor Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek (NWO).
